For each user record paired hit differences d=hit(candidate)−hit(baseline); macro improvement Δ=(1/4)Σ_dataset mean(d). Bootstrap 200 user pairs with replacement independently within each dataset, preserving model pairing and fixed candidate sets; recompute Δ over ~10,000 draws for a 95% interval. Report each dataset’s HR@10, difference, interval and discordant win/loss counts alongside macro results. One changed hit shifts dataset HR by 0.5 percentage points, macro HR by 0.125 points. [SciPy documents paired resampling](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html).

These intervals estimate user-sampling uncertainty under exchangeability assumptions, conditional on trained models and sampled candidates. They exclude training-seed variability, negative-sampling variability, dataset-to-dataset generalization and adaptive selection bias; few discordant users can produce unstable or degenerate intervals. With seeds fixed at 42, reruns measure reproducibility, not seed robustness. For the exact fixed benchmark, Δ is observed directly; population inference needs additional assumptions. Sampled HR cannot establish full-catalog ranking gains: sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

Recommended design: preregister a small hypothesis list, checkpoint schedule, practical improvement threshold and stopping rules; log every trial and validation query. An illustrative 43,200 GPU-second allocation: 8,640 baseline/calibration, 21,600 controlled single-factor ablations, 8,640 matched-budget finalist confirmation, 4,320 diagnostics/failures. Charge all four datasets and concurrent jobs cumulatively. Keep preprocessing seed=0, training/evaluation seeds=42, splits and evaluator unchanged. Reduce repeated validation peeking; treat searched-winner intervals as exploratory and freeze selection before independent held-out evaluation. Ordinary bootstrap or multiple-testing correction alone cannot repair adaptive search bias. [Cawley–Talbot](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html); [reusable-holdout research](https://research.ibm.com/publications/the-reusable-holdout-preserving-validity-in-adaptive-data-analysis).
